title: Crypto Profit & Loss Calculator
summary: See what a trade returns after buying and selling fees.
formula: Net profit = sale proceeds after fees − purchase cost including fees. ROI = profit ÷ purchase cost × 100.
note: Fees are percentages of trade value. Excludes taxes, funding, slippage and network costs. Use one consistent currency.
example: Buying 10 tokens at 100 and selling at 125 with 0.1% fees on each side produces 247.75 net profit.

title: Average Buy Price Calculator
summary: Combine purchases to find your average cost per token.
formula: Average cost = sum of quantity × price plus purchase fees, divided by total tokens.
note: Purchase fees are fixed amounts in your chosen quote currency. Assumes fees do not reduce the token quantity. Excludes sales and tax accounting.
example: Two tokens at 100 and one at 160, with no fees, have an average cost of 120.

title: Position Size Calculator
summary: Turn a risk budget and stop distance into a position size.
formula: Risk budget = balance × risk %. Units = risk budget ÷ absolute entry-to-stop distance.
note: Stops may fill at a worse price. Excludes fees, gaps and slippage. Notional can exceed available capital; this tool does not model margin or liquidation.
example: A 10,000 balance, 1% risk, 100 entry and 95 stop gives a risk budget of 100 and a size of 20 tokens.

title: Market Cap & FDV Calculator
summary: Compare circulating market value with a fully diluted estimate.
formula: Market cap = price × circulating supply. FDV = price × fully diluted supply assumption.
note: Enter the total or maximum supply you want to use for FDV. Supply definitions vary; name and verify your assumption. FDV holds price constant as supply increases.
example: A price of 2 with 10 million circulating and a 100 million diluted supply implies 20 million market cap and 200 million FDV.

title: Bitcoin Unit Converter
summary: Convert BTC, millibitcoin and satoshis without floating-point rounding.
note: Accepts plain decimal notation only. Values smaller than one satoshi are rejected instead of rounded. No fiat price is used.

title: Ethereum Unit Converter
summary: Convert ETH, gwei and wei with exact integer arithmetic.
note: Accepts plain decimal notation only. Values smaller than one wei are rejected instead of rounded. No fiat price is used.
example: 0.000000001 ETH is exactly 1 gwei, or 1,000,000,000 wei.

title: Ethereum Gas Fee Calculator
summary: Estimate a transaction fee from gas used and per-gas fees.
formula: Fee in ETH = gas used × (base fee + priority fee) ÷ 1,000,000,000.
note: Estimates Ethereum execution fees, excluding blob fees and extra L2 charges. Actual gas used can be lower than the gas limit. A simple ETH transfer often uses 21,000 gas; contract calls vary. Enter 0 for ETH price to omit USD.
example: 21,000 gas at 20 gwei base plus 2 gwei priority costs 0.000462 ETH.

title: Staking Rewards Simulator
summary: Explore hypothetical rewards with simple or compounded interest.
formula: Simple balance = principal × (1 + APR × days ÷ 365). Compounded balance = principal × (1 + APR ÷ n) ^ (n × days ÷ 365).
note: Constant APR assumption; fractional periods are interpolated. Rewards are in tokens, not fiat profit. Excludes fees, lockups, slashing, price changes and protocol rules. Yields are not guaranteed.
example: 1,000 tokens at 5% simple APR for 365 days produces 50 hypothetical reward tokens.

title: Portfolio Allocation Calculator
summary: Compare current weights with targets and plan a rebalance.
formula: Target value = portfolio total × target %. Adjustment = target value − current value.
note: Targets must sum to 100%. Rebalances at a fixed portfolio total with no added cash. Excludes fees, taxes and price movement. These targets are your inputs, not recommendations.
example: A 1,000 portfolio with 700 BTC and 300 ETH needs a 100 sale of BTC and 100 purchase of ETH to reach a 60/40 target.

title: Token Vesting Calculator
summary: Model an initial unlock followed by a linear vesting schedule.
formula: Initial tokens unlock at the start. Remaining tokens vest continuously after the cliff until the end. Total duration includes the cliff.
note: This model does not accumulate a catch-up release at the cliff. Dates use UTC midnight with month-end clamping. Actual contracts can use discrete releases or different cliff rules. Verify the project schedule.
example: 10,000 tokens, 10% initial, a three-month cliff and 12-month duration: at the end of month 12, all 10,000 tokens are unlocked.

title: Crypto Knowledge Quiz
summary: Test your understanding of wallets, fees and crypto fundamentals.
formula: Choose one answer for each question. Each correct answer earns one point.
note: Educational questions cover general concepts. Never enter wallet secrets into a quiz or calculator.
example: Review an explanation after every answer, then restart to try again.

title: Creator Campaign Planner
summary: Build a campaign quote and estimate your payout from your own rates.
formula: Brand quote = deliverables subtotal + usage uplift + exclusivity + reimbursed expenses. Creator payout = quote − commission on fees − production expenses.
note: Commission applies to fees including rights and exclusivity, excluding reimbursed production expenses. Excludes tax. All rates are supplied by you, not market benchmarks or guaranteed deals.
example: Two posts at 250, 20% usage rights, 100 expenses and 10% commission produces a 700 brand quote and 540 creator payout.
